messages:
alex: Heads-up — I'm prototyping a 'segmented audience' routing policy for runtime that splits traffic into seed / holdout / experiment buckets. Want quick feedback on safety checks before I wire telemetry and the console UI.

maria: SGTM. what are the failure modes you worry about?

alex: Main concerns: accidental 100% promotion, missing quota enforcement per-segment, and metric gaps when segs are small. Also need an easy rollback path.

drew: Can we reuse the existing quota token API? Prefer not to add a new store.

alex: Yes planning to use quota tokens but need a deterministic split key so tokens are stable across retries. thinking: hash(request.customer_id + experiment_id) mod 10000.

sam: How does this interact with model fallback? If primary variant OOMs we should reroute to baseline without touching seg assignment.

jen: +1 — separation of concerns is key. segment assignment should be pure and stored in request context; fallbacks read that but don't mutate.

alex: Example of the config I'm thinking of:

```yaml
routing_policy: segmented_audience_v1
params:
  seed_pct: 1.0      # percent for seed/QA
  experiment_pct: 10 # percent for active experiment
  holdout_pct: 89    # remainder
  seed_list: []      # explicit customer ids always seeded
  split_key: customer_id
  hash_mod: 10000
  per_segment_quota: true
  quota_namespace: "segmented-routing"

safety:
  max_promotion_pct: 20   # can't promote above this without approval
  telemetry_gate: true    # require telemetry warm-up before >seed_pct
  dry_run: true           # for first rollouts keep dry-run on
```

maria: telemetry_gate sounds good — what metrics do we require for warm-up?

alex: baseline: request_success_rate, median_p95_latency, model_error_rate, and token_cost_delta vs baseline. Need at least 24h and min 1000 seg requests.

drew: Can the console show segment-level charts side-by-side? Ops wants a quick glance for regressions.

jen: UI should surface when telemetry_gate blocks promotion and show link to logs/evals. Also allow manual override with audit log.

sam: ops-bot note: reminder to add quota alert: if segment burn rate > expected +/- 30% we should auto-throttle.

ops-bot: Deploy pipeline check: config with dry_run=true will be accepted but flagged. dry_run=false requires approval from eng-platform AND product-security.

alex: Implementation plan: 1) library for deterministic segment assignment (unit tested) 2) integrate with quota tokens 3) emit segment tag in telemetry and create dashboard panels 4) console controls for promotion & manual audit 5) rollout in dry-run then staged promotions.

maria: timeline?

alex: aiming for RFC this week, PR next Tue, dry-run on canary cluster in two weeks.

drew: Make sure the deterministic hash function is stable across languages (we have go + python runtimes). use xxhash64 with explicit seed.

alex: noted — I'll add that. anyone object to me creating a tiny dashboard prototype in grafana and a console mock?

jen: go for it. small request: add an 'eviction' policy if a segment exceeds quota for >5min — auto-shift traffic to holdout.

alex: good call. will include eviction TTL + cool-down window.

sam: thumbs up from SRE — just document alert thresholds.

alex: thanks everyone — will post the RFC link here when ready. :thumbsup:
